title: Estimate part lookup no longer offers a part once it is inactive
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an inactive part, part A, with 4 on hand and a hyphen in its part number.
  • Have an active part, part B, with 4 on hand, so the lookup has a part it must still offer.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, and descriptions that start with the same text, so one search finds both.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, that is still an estimate (it shows the Estimate pill), with a line, line 1, that reads Needs Approval and holds no parts.
  • Start on work order 1, on its Lines tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click Add Part under line 1.
  2. Type the shared start of the part numbers in the Part Number field.
  3. Replace the text with the shared start of the descriptions.
  4. Click the X at the top right of the window.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Part Request window opens for line 1 of work order 1, with the Part Number field.

Step 2:

  • Part B is offered.
  • No row for part A is offered: neither an inventory row with "Inventory Qty" nor a "Part Library" row.

Step 3:

  • Part B is offered.
  • Again no row for part A is offered.

Step 4:

  • The window closes; line 1 still holds no parts and work order 1 still shows the Estimate pill.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S9-R2: “Part lookup on an estimate line does not return inactive parts.”

From: Jira tickets and comments under epic SV-10647 (saved in sources/jira-2026-10-27/ALL-TICKETS-2026-10-27.md), read 27 Oct 2026

  • SV-10822 acceptance criteria: “Given GREASETUBE is inactive, when the user searches "GREASE" on a work order, estimate, part sale, purchase order or technician charge-out, then it is not offered, neither as an inventory part nor as a Part Library entry.”
